Sodium valproate has been used in the management of Cushing’s syndrome (p.2344). Epilepsy. Valproate is one of the drugs of choice in partial sei- zures, primary generalised tonic-clonic seizures, absence sei- zures, and myoclonic seizures (see p.465), although evidence for some of these is lacking. It is also the drug of choice in epileptic syndromes such as the Lennox-Gastaut syndrome because of its wide therapeutic spectrum, and it may be useful in tonic or atonic seizures and infantile spasms.
